{COMMON_DEFS}
Threading Architecture: Platform Threads (1:1) vs Java 21 Virtual Threads (M:N) Heavyweight OS kernel threads with 1MB stacks vs lightweight JVM user-mode continuations mounted on Carrier ForkJoinPool
Platform Threads (1:1 OS Thread Model)
• OS Kernel Thread Binding: - 1 Java Thread = 1 OS Kernel Thread - Fixed stack size: ~1MB reserved per thread - Max ~3,000 threads before OS OOM limit
• Blocking Socket I/O Penalty: - When thread blocks on DB / HTTP read: - Entire OS thread goes to SLEEP (Context Switch) - CPU cores sit idle while thread pools starve
High Memory & Kernel Context Switch Overhead
Virtual Threads: Project Loom (M:N User Model)
• User-Mode Continuations: - Managed directly by JVM (Millions per JVM) - Dynamic stack: ~1KB initial memory on heap - Mounted on Carrier Threads (ForkJoinPool)
• Non-Blocking I/O Unmounting: - When blocking I/O occurs, virtual thread UNMOUNTS - Carrier thread immediately executes next task! - Restored to carrier when I/O completes (epoll)
High Concurrency: 1,000,000+ Concurrent Requests
